note: Two gates with different jobs. The per-seed ceilings are the 100th percentile plus ~20% headroom and catch catastrophic breakage of a single instrument. The mean gate is much tighter and is the sensitive one: a systematic regression moves the mean long before it pushes any single seed past its ceiling. Mean level offset is -0.11 dB, so no residual gain error remains.

knownOutlier.detail: One oscillator with delay and FM, no reverb. Peak level matches Chrome to 0.00 dB, so the instrument is not mis-levelled; the divergence is in the delay tail. Not yet attributed. It is the only seed above 6.1 dB, and the mean is unaffected.

sustainedCalibration.note: Same policy as the one-shot gates: per-seed ceilings at roughly the worst measured plus 20%, and a tighter mean that a systematic regression moves first. The sustained mean sits close to the one-shot 2.28 dB, which is the point -- the held path is no worse than the path that was already covered.
sustainedCalibration.rmsCeilingNote: The RMS ceiling is driven entirely by seed 1804795437, the same known outlier as the one-shot set, at 45.0 dB in both. Every other seed is under 8.4 dB. That seed diverges in its delay tail, which the RMS envelope metric is far more sensitive to than the mel distance -- its mel is only 4.2 dB.
